messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: CRITICAL — canary-service-5xx-rate high in us-west-2. threshold=5% over 2m. triggered by canary-traffic-checker. link: https://console.redwood.ai/alerts/3642 :pagerduty:

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident #PD-9221 created and paged escalation policy 'infra-oncall'. Auto-escalation in 5m if unacknowledged.

amy (oncall): acked PD-9221. jumping in — grabbing logs + canary graph.

sam (release-owner): on it — this rollout started 3m ago, new quant kernel + batching changes. I'm going to stop new canary traffic if possible.

mira: I see a spike in 5xx on the model-serving pods (canary replica set). p99 latency also up ~700ms. first error is 'kv-cache-miss + OOM-retry' in the logs. paste: ```2026-03-14T21:02:12Z canary-0 container stderr: Error: failed to allocate kv cache shard: out of memory```

jordan: can we shift canary traffic back to stable? I can flip the traffic-split in traffic-controller. command: `rc traffic set canary=0 stable=100 --namespace=prod-us-west`

lee_ops: preemptively scaling down canary replicas to 0 to stop error noise. running: `kubectl scale rs canary-abc --replicas=0 -n prod-us-west`

sam (release-owner): paused rollout in CI/CD and cancelling remaining canary jobs. also starting rollback to previous image. cc @mira for verification.

amy (oncall): good. i've muted the alert rule for canary 10m to avoid noisy paging while we confirm mitigation. tagging incident as 'deploy-triggered'.

eva: quick customer-impact check: Console shows 0.8% of total requests from customers in us-west returned 5xx in last 2m. no major accounts flagged but SLO error budget will take a hit if this persists.

mira: logs show the runtime kernel path hitting a path that allocates a larger kv-cache shard size when sequence_len > 1024 — that aligns with a change in the quant batching heuristic from the rollout.

jordan: rolling back the Deployment now: `kubectl rollout undo deploy/canary-service -n prod-us-west --to-revision=37`. monitoring events.

incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD-9221 acknowledged by amy (oncall). escalation paused.

sam (release-owner): rollback initiated and verified: new pods are terminating, previous revision pods are coming up. connecting tracing to verify request flow.

lee_ops: traffic-split flipped back to stable. confirmed stable pods handling 100% traffic. canary replicas at 0.

amy (oncall): observing metrics — 5xx rate dropping. p95 latency returning to baselines.

eva: customer impact estimate updated: peak error rate impacted ~0.9% of infer requests for ~6 minutes, estimated % of sessions affected <0.5%. no active support tickets so far.

mira: leaving notes for postmortem: root cause likely quant-batching change causing transient kv-cache allocation > node memory. mitigation: revert heuristic and add canary memory headroom guard.

sam (release-owner): follow-up actions I'm owning: revert commit (PR #612), add canary resource guard in deployment template, add canary-only memory OOM alert and a faker traffic test for sequence_len>1024.

amy (oncall): handing off to mira for post-incident follow-up. i'm going offline in 10m.

mira: thanks — i'll take it. leaving the channel to collect artifacts: logs, pod events, console graphs. tagging this incident for a 1hr async review and 24h postmortem slot.

incident-bot: PD-9221: incident resolved by amy (oncall). resolution reason: rollback to previous revision + traffic re-route. duration 00:12:08.

amy (oncall): closing thread. brief summary for ops notes: canary rollout caused kv-cache OOM path for certain sequences, triggered 5xx spike ~0.9% requests in us-west-2, rollback and reroute mitigated impact within 12m. follow-ups: PR revert, canary resource guard, add targeted alerting.

sam (release-owner): thanks team. will file the postmortem and link here when ready. :thumbsup:
